body.description: n8n webhook request body, exactly as the user prescribed (AAP 0.3.3). Sent with Content-Type: application/json and the shared-secret header {N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET_HEADER}: {N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET}; the secret value is never recorded. Exactly these three keys: no Google client id, client secret, refresh token, developer token or login-customer-id is ever sent, because they live only in n8n's credential store. n8n's Google Ads node runs the query as the native REST call POST https://googleads.googleapis.com/v25/customers/{customerId}/googleAds:search, whose body is camelCase {query, pageToken}; the snake_case customer_id and page_token here are the n8n envelope the user prescribed. The native pageSize (deprecated; rejected with PAGE_SIZE_NOT_SUPPORTED), validateOnly and searchSettings are never sent.

customer_id.description: Google Ads customer id: 10 digits, no dashes (GOOGLE_ADS_CUSTOMER_ID); the native {customerId} path parameter.

query.description: One GAQL query per call; googleAds:search v25, never searchStream. Always one of the templates Q-G1..Q-G8 or Q-G2b in connectors/google_n8n/queries.py; the response rows follow the row_*.json contract chosen by payloads.row_surface_for(query).

page_token.description: null on a first-page call; otherwise the nextPageToken of the previous response, sent back at once because page tokens expire after a few hours. The native pageToken.

body.description: Synchronous n8n response: the SearchGoogleAdsResponse of n8n's Google Ads node running googleAds:search v25 (AAP 0.3.3), with camelCase keys. totalResultsCount and summaryRow are not declared: they are returned only when requested through searchSettings, which the three-key envelope cannot send. Array wrapper: the parser also accepts a one-element JSON array wrapping this object (n8n's "all incoming items" response mode) and unwraps it before validation. Completeness: a response with fewer than 10,000 rows is complete; a response carrying nextPageToken is followed at once; exactly 10,000 rows with no token has unknown completeness, and the connector partitions the query: keyset scans (ORDER BY id, id > last id, LIMIT 9999) for Q-G2, Q-G4 and Q-G7, and date, campaign.id and ad_group.id range halving for Q-G3, Q-G5 and Q-G6. A capped single (day, ad group) partition of Q-G6 is stored as returned and marked incomplete (AAP 0.3.3). Body-level errors: n8n may return a Google error with HTTP 200. It is not a success body and no error schema is declared here; connectors/errors.classify reads it. Google's documented error format (Understand API errors, last updated 2026-09-30) is a google.rpc Status {code, message, details[]} whose optional details[] holds a GoogleAdsFailure {"@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.ads.googleads.v25.errors.GoogleAdsFailure", errors[] {errorCode {<camelCase error type>: <enum>}, message, trigger, location, details {quotaErrorDetails {rateScope, rateName, retryDelay}}}, requestId}; retryDelay, a Duration such as "30s", is the transient wait when no Retry-After header is sent. It arrives in one of two shapes, and the classifier reads both, also inside the one-element array: the REST error envelope {"error": {code: <HTTP status>, message, status: <google.rpc code name>, details[]}}, whose error.code is an HTTP status; or a bare google.rpc Status {code: <numeric google.rpc code>, message, details[]} relayed as the whole body, recognised when it carries neither results nor fieldMask and its code is a google.rpc.Code from 1 to 16. PERMISSION_DENIED (google.rpc code 7, HTTP 403) and UNAUTHENTICATED (code 16, HTTP 401), and the error types AuthorizationError and AuthenticationError, mean access denied (switch to simulated); RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 8, HTTP 429) is transient (retry, then stale); QueryError is a defect. Every other numeric google.rpc code classifies like the HTTP status google.rpc.Code maps it to: for example INVALID_ARGUMENT (code 3, HTTP 400) is a defect and UNAVAILABLE (code 14, HTTP 503) is transient. Observed n8n behaviour (2026-10-07): an invalid GAQL query returns HTTP 500 {"message": "Error in workflow"} with no Google error body, so at the HTTP level a query defect is indistinguishable from a transient 5xx.

results.description: REST GoogleAdsRow objects with camelCase keys; int64 values (ids, *Micros, impressions, clicks) arrive as strings. At most 10,000 rows per page. ABSENT (not an empty array) when the query matches zero rows: an empty Search result is {fieldMask, queryResourceConsumption} (Google Ads Developer Blog, 2025-07-01); the client treats absent results with fieldMask present as zero rows.

items.description: One row. Its shape is governed by the row_*.json contract of this query (payloads.row_surface_for(query)); left open here because the envelope carries every query.

fieldMask.description: Comma-joined camelCase paths of the selected fields, e.g. adGroupCriterion.keyword.text,adGroupCriterion.status. Present on every successful response, including zero-row responses; a body with neither results nor fieldMask is a QueryDefect.

queryResourceConsumption.description: int64 resource units consumed to serve the query. The v25 reference types it as a string in int64 format, as proto3 JSON renders int64, while Google's 2025-07-01 blog example shows the number 123, so both are accepted. Returned for zero-row responses too since August 2025. Not required, so a live capture without it still validates. Informational only; not the quota.

nextPageToken.description: Present only when more pages exist (more than 10,000 rows); not returned for the last page. Sent back at once as page_token, because page tokens expire after a few hours. Not observed in live n8n responses.

metricAttributes.description: The metric attributes of the metrics in the results (v25 reference; present since v23). Unlike totalResultsCount and summaryRow it is not gated by searchSettings, so it is declared and a response carrying it still validates. Not observed in live n8n responses (2026-10-07) and never read by the connector.

items.description: MetricAttributes: one metric and its attributes.
MetricAttributes.Attribute: one attribute as a key-value pair.
